The manipulation of time in this excerpt (which is the opening of Stefan Zweig's novella *Der Amokläufer*) is balanced and serves the narrative purpose effectively. 

First, the author uses **compression of time** to quickly establish the setting and the narrator's growing frustration. The process of booking the ticket over two days and the subsequent three monotonous, suffocating days aboard the crowded ship are condensed into just a few paragraphs. This rapid summarization effectively conveys the repetitive, claustrophobic nature of the voyage without boring the reader with hour-by-hour accounts of mundane ship life.

Then, the author shifts to **stretching of time** once the narrator wakes up after midnight and goes up to the empty deck. A single, quiet moment of looking up at the night sky is drawn out through rich, sensory descriptions of the stars, the moonlight, and the silhouettes of the ship. This deliberate slowing down of the pacing creates a stark, peaceful contrast to the chaotic daytime scenes and builds a mysterious, suspended atmosphere that prepares the reader for the "strange episode" hinted at in the very first paragraph.
